title: Type Juggling and Loose Comparison Bypasses
platform_conditions: PHP 8.x default configuration; PHP 8 tightened string<->int comparisons, but two numeric strings still compare numerically, so '0e'-prefixed digest collisions persist
security_mechanism: PHP's == converts operands before comparing: two numeric strings are compared as numbers, so any md5/sha1 digest of the form '0e' followed by all digits (magic hashes, e.g. md5('240610708') == '0e462097431906509030567485623617') equals every other such digest because both cast to float 0. in_array() and array_search() default to loose comparison unless the third $strict argument is true, and switch() matches loosely, so membership/role checks pass on unexpected values. On PHP 7, passing an array to strcmp()/strlen() raises a warning and returns NULL, which == treats as equal to 0, letting an attacker-supplied array bypass the check (PHP 8 throws a TypeError instead).

source_sink_clues.source: Request-supplied digests, tokens, role/flag parameters, and array-vs-scalar parameter shapes (a[]= style) that flow into comparison constructs.
source_sink_clues.sink: === vs == distinctions aside: == / != on authenticators; in_array / array_search without $strict=true; switch matching attacker-controlled scalars; strcmp/strlen receiving attacker-chosen argument types

tracking_guards: Require hash_equals() or password_verify() for every authenticator comparison; require in_array(..., true) strict mode on security paths; require gettype()/is_string() checks before functions that expect scalars; prefer === / !== everywhere an authentication outcome is decided.
not_candidate_when: Operands are provably the same internal type by construction (both server-generated integers), the comparison is === / !==, digest comparison already goes through hash_equals/password_verify, or in_array is strict=true and feeds a non-security decision.
